title: Extension bounds for Frobenius modules
statement:
Let $0\to V'\to V\to V''\to 0$ be an exact sequence of Frobenius
modules. If $V'$ and $V''$ are mixed of weights at most $w$, then
$V$ is mixed of weights at most $w$.

proof.text: Unpack the two finite stable filtrations from [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. Define W_i=f(V_i) for i<=m and W_i=g^(-1)(Z_(i-m)) for i>m. Exactness identifies f(V_m)=range(f)=ker(g)=g^(-1)(Z_0). Thus the definitions agree at the join. The zero and whole endpoints, increasing property and Frobenius stability follow from those of V and Z and the equivariance of f and g. The construction permits m=0 or n=0 and repeated steps.

For a surjective equivariant linear map between upper subspaces whose inverse image of the lower target subspace is the lower source subspace, the induced quotient map is bijective: its kernel is zero and representatives lift by surjectivity. Conjugate the pure target quotient Frobenius through this linear equivalence. Equivariance gives the prescribed quotient action, and applying the equivalence to a nonzero eigenvector proves that purity is preserved. This elementary quotient argument is the fully proved private helper transport_piece.

For each mapped filtration step, injectivity of f identifies its upper subspace with V_(i+1) and identifies its lower subspace with V_i; use the inverse restricted equivalence in transport_piece. For each pulled-back step, the restriction of g is surjective onto Z_(j+1) and the preimage of Z_j is the lower subspace; apply transport_piece directly. All weights are inherited unchanged and remain <=w. Hence W satisfies every clause of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], giving mixedness of B.
